description: The Commodity Flow Survey is the primary source of national and state-level data on domestic freight shipments by American businesses. As a shipper-based survey it records how establishments move raw materials and finished goods: the commodity (SCTG code), mode of transportation, value, weight, origin and destination of shipments, including exports; it excludes imports and shipments from US territories, and covers mining, manufacturing, wholesale, selected retail and services and some auxiliary establishments. It is a joint effort of the Census Bureau and the Bureau of Transportation Statistics, required by law, with 165,000 establishments sampled for 2022, each reporting shipments from one week per quarter. Coverage is national, by state and CFS area, with datasets for 2012, 2017 and 2022; the 2022 data were released on 26 June 2025 and the 2022 Public Use Microdata Sample (a 680 MB CSV of shipment records) in January 2026. Tables are free downloads in XLS, CSV and PDF. Caveats: noise infusion protects respondents, the survey runs every five years, and imports are out of scope. The CFS supports network flow and capacity planning studies of freight, supply-chain and resilience analysis and model calibration, and is the base of the Freight Analysis Framework catalogued here, which complements it with other sectors and forecasts.
